title: Verbs That Change Meaning: stop, try, remember, forget, regret, go on
grammarTitle: Gerund vs Infinitive: Six Verbs That Change Meaning
grammarNote: Шесть самых важных глаголов, после которых выбор герундия или инфинитива МЕНЯЕТ СМЫСЛ. Это один из самых сложных и самых важных аспектов грамматики на уровне B1-B2. Понимание этих различий — признак подлинного мастерства в английском.

grammarTable.subject: STOP + gerund
grammarTable.example: "She stopped smoking." (the habit ended) / "I stopped working at 6." ✅

grammarTable.subject: STOP + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "She stopped to smoke." (stopped something else in order to smoke) ✅

grammarTable.subject: TRY + gerund
grammarTable.example: "Try adding salt." (experiment with this) / "I tried swimming." ✅

grammarTable.subject: TRY + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "I tried to swim." (made effort; possibly didn't manage) ✅

grammarTable.subject: REMEMBER + gerund
grammarTable.example: "I remember meeting her." (I have a memory of it — it happened) ✅

grammarTable.subject: REMEMBER + inf.
grammarTable.example: "Remember to call him." (don't forget this future task) ✅

grammarTable.subject: FORGET + gerund
grammarTable.example: "I've forgotten meeting her." (I met her but have no memory) ✅

grammarTable.subject: FORGET + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "I forgot to call him." (I was supposed to but didn't) ✅

grammarTable.subject: REGRET + gerund
grammarTable.example: "I regret telling her." (I told her — now feel sorry) ✅

grammarTable.subject: REGRET + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "I regret to inform you..." (formal — introducing what follows) ✅

grammarTable.subject: GO ON + gerund
grammarTable.example: "He went on talking for an hour." (continued talking) ✅

grammarTable.subject: GO ON + infinitive
grammarTable.example: "She went on to become famous." (progressed to a new stage) ✅

rows.example: "He stopped working." (he no longer works) ✅
"He stopped to work." (he stopped [other thing] in order to work) ✅
"She stopped running." (running stopped ✅) / "She stopped to run." (something else stopped → she ran) ✅

rows.form: Common error: ✗ stop to smoke = quit
rows.example: ✅ "She stopped SMOKING" = quit. "She stopped TO SMOKE" = paused to have a cigarette. ✅
"Try adding more sugar." (experiment with this adjustment) ✅
"I tried to add sugar but the jar was sealed." (effort; difficulty implied) ✅
"If you have a headache, try drinking water." (experiment with this remedy) ✅
"Despite being tired, she tried to finish the report." (effort against difficulty) ✅
"I remember swimming in the Caspian as a child." (memory of past event) ✅
"Remember to lock the door!" / "I forgot to call him." (future/unfulfilled obligation) ✅

rows.form: Test: has the event happened yet?
rows.example: "I remember meeting him" → yes, happened. "I remember to meet him" → not yet, future task. ✅
"I've forgotten meeting him." (unusual but grammatically correct: I met him, have no memory) ✅

grammarExtra.title: REGRET and GO ON: past/future and continuation/progression

rows.form: Regret + gerund = sorry about past action
rows.example: "I regret saying that." (I said it — now feel sorry) ✅

rows.form: Regret + infinitive = formal intro of bad news
rows.example: "We regret to announce that..." / "I regret to say..." ✅ (formal; introducing what follows)
"She went on working despite being exhausted." (continued the same activity) ✅

rows.form: Go on + infinitive = PROGRESS to next stage
rows.example: "After graduating, she went on to become a professor." (new stage of life) ✅

grammarExtra.title: ❌ Most common errors with meaning-change pairs

rows.form: ✗ "I stopped to work." (meaning: I quit work)
rows.example: ✅ "I stopped WORKING." — to quit work = gerund. "Stopped TO work" = paused in order to work. ✅
✅ "Remember MEETING her." (gerund) OR "Remember TO MEET her." (infinitive) — not mixed. ✅
✅ "We regret TO INFORM you that..." — formal announcement = regret + infinitive. ✅
✅ "She went on WORKING." (gerund, no "to") OR "She went on TO BECOME." (to + base form, not gerund). ✅

grammarTip:
Six verbs that CHANGE MEANING:

STOP:
STOP + gerund = activity ENDS: "She stopped SMOKING."
STOP + infinitive = purpose: "She stopped TO SMOKE."

TRY:
TRY + gerund = experiment: "Try ADDING salt."
TRY + infinitive = effort (may fail): "I tried TO SWIM."

REMEMBER / FORGET:
gerund = PAST memory: "I remember MEETING her."
infinitive = FUTURE task: "Remember TO CALL him."

REGRET:
gerund = sorry about PAST: "I regret TELLING her."
infinitive = formal intro: "I regret TO INFORM you..."

GO ON:
gerund = CONTINUE same: "She went on TALKING."
infinitive = PROGRESS to new: "She went on TO BECOME famous."

exercises.text: "He was cycling along the river. He stopped ___ admire the view."
exercises.hint: "Stopped TO ADMIRE" = he stopped cycling in order to admire the view (purpose). ✅
"Stopped SMOKING" = the habit ended. She no longer smokes. ✅

exercises.text: "If the WiFi is slow, ___ restarting the router." (as a remedy to test)
exercises.hint: "TRY RESTARTING the router." — experiment with this as a solution. "Try out" meaning. ✅

exercises.text: "She was so exhausted that she couldn't ___ even one more step."
exercises.hint: "TRY TO WALK" — effort against difficulty (she's exhausted). ✅

exercises.text: "Don't forget ___ submit your assignment before midnight."
"I can't believe she was at that conference. I ___ (remember / see) her there."
exercises.hint: "I remember SEEING her there." — memory of a past event. GERUND after "remember" for past. ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (forget) that we had already met. She seemed familiar for some reason."
opts: Both "forgot meeting" and "forgot having met" work
exercises.correct: Both "forgot meeting" and "forgot having met" work
exercises.hint: "forgot MEETING her" ✅ / "forgot HAVING MET her" ✅ (perfect gerund for past event before forgetting). ✅

exercises.text: "We ___ (regret) ___ (inform) you that your application has been unsuccessful."
opts: Both are correct in formal English
exercises.hint: "We REGRET TO INFORM you..." — formal letter formula. Regret + infinitive for bad news announcement. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ (regret) ___ (not / tell) him the truth when she had the chance."
exercises.hint: "She REGRETS NOT TELLING him." — past action she wishes she'd done differently. Gerund. ✅

exercises.text: "Despite the rain, the musicians went on ___ the concert."
exercises.hint: "Went on PLAYING the concert." — continued the same activity despite the rain. ✅

exercises.text: "After completing her undergraduate degree, she went on ___ a PhD."
exercises.hint: "Went on TO STUDY a PhD." — progressed to a new stage of life/career. ✅

exercises.text: "I tried ___ (call) her several times but she didn't answer." (effort, possible failure)
exercises.hint: "I TRIED TO CALL her." — effort toward a goal (calling) that didn't succeed (she didn't answer). ✅

exercises.text: "I remember locking the door." — this means:
opts: I need to lock the door
I have a memory of locking the door (it's done)
I forgot to lock the door
exercises.correct: I have a memory of locking the door (it's done)
exercises.hint: "Remember + gerund (locking)" = past memory. The locking happened; I have a memory of it. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ working, even though everyone had gone home." (continued)
exercises.hint: "She went on WORKING." — continued the same activity. Go on + gerund = continuation. ✅

exercises.text: "I regret ___ (not / apply) for the scholarship earlier."
opts: Both "not applying" and "not having applied" are correct
exercises.correct: Both "not applying" and "not having applied" are correct
exercises.hint: "Regret not APPLYING for the scholarship." ✅ / "Regret not HAVING APPLIED for the scholarship." ✅ (perfect gerund for prior past action). Both correct. ✅

exercises.text: "After years of trying ___ quit, she finally stopped ___ and never went back." (a) to b) + (c) to smoke or d) smoking?)
exercises.hint: "Trying TO QUIT" (effort toward goal) + "stopped SMOKING" (activity ended). ✅

questions.text: "He stopped to answer his phone." — What did he do?
opts: He stopped what he was doing in order to answer his phone
questions.correct: He stopped what he was doing in order to answer his phone
questions.hint: "Stop + infinitive" = purpose. He stopped [something else] in order to answer. ✅

questions.text: "She stopped answering his messages." — What happened?
questions.hint: "Stop + gerund" = activity ENDS. She no longer answers his messages. ✅

questions.text: "Try adding vinegar to the dressing." — What does this suggest?
opts: Experiment with this — see if it helps
questions.correct: Experiment with this — see if it helps
questions.hint: "Try + gerund" = experiment. "Try ADDING vinegar" = test this remedy/adjustment. ✅

questions.text: "I tried to open the jar but it was too tight." — "tried to open" implies:
opts: I made an effort but probably failed
I chose not to open it
questions.correct: I made an effort but probably failed
questions.hint: "Try + infinitive" = effort toward a goal (possibly not achieved). The jar was too tight → probably failed. ✅

questions.text: "I remember locking the door." vs "I remember to lock the door." — key difference?
opts: "Locking" = past memory; "to lock" = future task I don't forget
questions.correct: "Locking" = past memory; "to lock" = future task I don't forget
questions.hint: Gerund = past memory. Infinitive = future obligation you keep in mind. ✅

questions.text: "I forgot to meet him." — What happened?
opts: I met him but have no memory
I was supposed to meet him but didn't
I don't want to meet him
questions.correct: I was supposed to meet him but didn't
questions.hint: "Forget + infinitive" = failure to do something you were supposed to. ✅

questions.text: "We regret to announce that the event has been cancelled." — "to announce" because:
opts: "Regret + infinitive" introduces formal bad news that follows
questions.correct: "Regret + infinitive" introduces formal bad news that follows
questions.hint: "Regret + infinitive" = formal introduction of bad news. The announcing is about what follows. ✅

questions.text: "I regret saying that." — What does this mean?
opts: I'm going to say something bad
I said it and now feel sorry
I plan to say something soon
questions.correct: I said it and now feel sorry
questions.hint: "Regret + gerund" = the action is in the past; you feel remorse about it. ✅

questions.text: "She went on to write three more novels." — What does this mean?
opts: She continued writing the same novel
She progressed to a new stage — wrote more novels after this point
She wrote three novels and then went on holiday
She tried to write three more novels
questions.correct: She progressed to a new stage — wrote more novels after this point
questions.hint: "Go on + infinitive" = progression to a new activity or stage. ✅

questions.text: "Despite the interruptions, she went on explaining." — What happened?
opts: She moved to a new topic
She continued with the same explanation
questions.correct: She continued with the same explanation
questions.hint: "Go on + gerund" = CONTINUE the same activity. ✅

opts: "We regret informing you that the event was cancelled." (formal letter)
"She stopped to smoke" (meaning: she quit smoking)
questions.correct: None of these — all have errors
questions.hint: All have errors: "regret to inform" not "informing"; "stopped smoking" = quit; "forgot meeting" not "to meeting"; "remember to call" not "to calling." ✅

questions.text: Which correctly expresses: "She was supposed to lock the door but didn't"?
questions.hint: "Forgot TO LOCK the door." = forget + infinitive for a task you were supposed to do. ✅
